title: nebra.toml
description: The configuration of a Nebra project.

name.description: The project name. Used as the package name when the project is a dependency, and in generated documentation.

version.description: The project version. Version ranges such as `^1.2` work when it looks like semver.

target.description: The Lua dialect the compiler emits. It decides which operators and library calls the generated code may use.
enumDescriptions: Lua 5.1
Lua 5.2
Lua 5.3
Lua 5.4
LuaJIT

entry.description: The Nebra file `nebra run` and `nebra compile` start from.

extends.description: Other configuration files, relative to this one, loaded as a baseline before this file's keys override them.

preset.description: A rule preset loaded before this file. `strict` turns on every type-safety rule; `relaxed` enforces none.
enumDescriptions: strict_nil, immutable_default and exhaustive_match = "explicit", without allow_any
Plain Lua with types, no rules enforced

source.description: The directory the compiler reads `.neb` sources from. Imports are relative to it.

output.description: The directory the generated Lua is written to.

minify.description: Strip whitespace and comments from the generated Lua.

generate_docs.description: Also generate the documentation site on `nebra build`, as `nebra docs` does.

source_maps.description: Write a `.lua.map` next to every generated file, mapping its lines to the `.neb` source, so a host can translate tracebacks.

generate_declarations.description: Also emit `.d.neb` declarations on `nebra build`, so other projects can type-check against this one.

globals.description: Directories or `.d.neb` files whose declarations are loaded into every file, such as the API of a game engine.

annotations.description: Directories or `.neb` files holding annotation plugins.

types_only.description: The project ships only `.d.neb` declarations. `nebra build`, `compile`, `run` and `test` do nothing.

runtime_global.description: The global this package is reachable as at runtime, for runtimes where another package cannot load its files. Its root module sets the global from its exports, and `import { X } from "<package>"` in a consumer reads `Global.X` instead of loading a file.

runtime_export.description: How the root module sets `runtime_global`: `%name` stands for the quoted global name and `%value` for the exports, such as `"Package.Export(%name, %value)"` in nanos world.

assets.description: Files copied into the output. Keys are paths from the project root, values paths in the output.

dependencies.description: Packages the project needs at runtime, by name. A value is a specifier such as `"github:owner/repo@v1"` or a table like `{ git = "...", tag = "v1" }`.

dev_dependencies.description: Packages needed only locally and in CI; left out of published packages.

peer_dependencies.description: Packages the consumer of this package has to provide; checked but not installed.

sides.description: Which sides the files matching each glob may use: `"src/Client/**" = ["client", "shared"]`. Declarations marked `@side(...)` are only reachable from matching files.

enumDescriptions: Code that runs on the client
Code that runs on the server
Code that runs on both

code.description: How the generated Lua is written.

index_base.description: The first index of a list. `0` shifts every index by one so lists start at 0; `1` keeps Lua's indexing.

concat_operator.description: An operator that concatenates strings in addition to `..`.

semicolons.description: Whether statements may, must or must not end with `;`.

import_statement.description: What an import becomes in Lua; `%s` stands for the quoted module path, such as `'Package.Require(%s)'`.

import_extension.description: A suffix added to every imported module path, such as `".lua"` for loaders that need it.

import_path.description: How imports of the project's own modules are written: as in the source, or as the normalized path from the output root, such as `Server/types/Calendar`, for loaders that cache modules under the path they are given.
enumDescriptions: The path as the source writes it, such as `../types/Calendar`
The path from the output root, such as `Server/types/Calendar`

strip_unused.description: Leave unused locals, functions and imports out of the generated Lua.

libs.description: Further directories imports are resolved in.

auto_imports.description: Modules imported into every file as a namespace named after their last path segment.

auto_imports_emit.description: Emit the `require` of the automatic imports. Turn off when the runtime loads those modules itself.

mangle.description: Renaming symbols to short names to shrink the output.

mangle_top_level.description: Rename top-level names too, which are the public surface of the output.

keep_function_names.description: Keep the names of functions, which code outside the output may look up by name.

rules.description: How strictly the compiler checks types.

allow_any.description: Allow the `any` type. When off, every type has to be spelled out.

strict_nil.description: Assigning `nil` to a type not marked with `?` is an error.

immutable_default.description: Locals are immutable unless declared `local mut`.

deep_freeze.description: With `immutable_default`, also freeze the tables immutable locals refer to, at a runtime cost.

exhaustive_match.description: How strictly `if` chains and `match` over unions and enums have to cover every case.
enumDescriptions: No check
An else branch covers the rest
Every case needs its own branch

stdlib.description: The declarations of the standard Lua library.

enabled.description: Load the standard library declarations. Turn off for runtimes without the Lua globals.

disabled.description: Names to remove: a global or library such as `"io"`, or one member such as `"string.dump"`.

scripts.description: Shell commands run at points of the build and install.

pre_install.description: Run before this package is linked as a dependency; only with `nebra install --allow-scripts`.

post_install.description: Run after this package is linked as a dependency; only with `nebra install --allow-scripts`.

linker.description: How packages from the global store are placed in `nebra_modules/`.
enumDescriptions: A symlink on Unix, a junction on Windows
Always a symlink
Always a directory junction
A physical copy

allow_scripts.description: Let dependencies run their install scripts.

dirs.description: Directories whose every `.neb` file is a test; the source directory is always searched as well.

patterns.description: File name endings that mark a test file outside the test directories.

quiet.description: Print only the summary, not a line per test.

reflection.description: Which declarations runtime reflection can describe.

enumDescriptions: Every class, interface, enum, function and variable
Only declarations marked @reflectable
Nothing; reflection is left out entirely
